Count Ugolino pauses from gnawing Archbishop Ruggieri's head to recount how Ruggieri imprisoned him with his sons and grandsons in a tower, where they starved. Farther on, traitors to guests lie face upward with tears frozen over their eyes; Fra Alberigo explains that some such souls fall to Hell before their bodies die. At the center of the lake stands the gigantic, three-faced Lucifer, whose wings generate the freezing wind and whose mouths chew Judas, Brutus, and Cassius. Virgil climbs down Lucifer with Dante and passes the earth's center, where their direction reverses. They ascend a hidden passage and finally emerge from Hell beneath the stars.

characters.description: Captain of Omega and leader of its human refugees. He directs raids on Ornu prison mines, balancing the rescue of enslaved people against danger to the ship and the civilians already aboard.
characters.name: Bill Henderson

characters.description: A senior officer aboard Omega who monitors the heat and structural risks created by repeated short-range jumps. Her calculations and operational advice are central to the prison-mine campaign.
characters.name: Bina Chakravarti

characters.description: The Marine commander responsible for extracting prisoners from the asteroid mine. He leads Omega's ground force into hostile facilities while the ship fights outside.
characters.name: Alden Stone

characters.description: An ancient, sentient warship that shelters humanity's refugees and carries out their rescue campaign. Its short-range jump system offers a major tactical advantage but risks severe damage when used repeatedly.
characters.name: Omega

characters.description: Omega's envoy and adviser within a simulated environment. Val calculates the danger posed by the ship's jump drive and helps Bill understand Omega's limits.
characters.name: Val

characters.description: A lieutenant returning to Omega's bridge after an illness contracted in an Ornu prison camp. He served with Bill before the rebellion and resumes duty while still recovering.
characters.name: James Riding

characters.description: Bill's father, identified as a long-term prisoner in an Ornu camp. His captivity links the liberation campaign directly to Bill's family.
characters.name: Gordon Henderson

characters.description: The pilot of the Marines' extraction can during the mine assault. Splat keeps the craft ready while Stone's team searches for surviving prisoners.
characters.name: Splat

characters.description: The Ornu ruler who holds Pertinax responsible for failing to destroy Omega. He accepts Pertinax's proposal to blame Philo for the widening crisis and orders the consul's execution.
characters.name: Ornu emperor

characters.description: An Ornu imperator whose standing is endangered after failing to destroy Omega. He survives the emperor's scrutiny by presenting his retreat as an act of loyalty.
characters.name: Pertinax

characters.description: An Ornu consul whom Pertinax proposes as a public scapegoat for the widening political crisis. His family connection to an escaped former Signifier makes him useful to the emperor.
characters.name: Philo

characters.name: Former Signifier

characters.description: Bill's mother and Gordon's wife. She helps receive the traumatized survivors of a failed mine rescue and supports continuing the effort to free people still held by the Ornu.
characters.name: Miriam Henderson

characters.description: The British prime minister speaks for civilians demanding a secure settlement and opposes Bill’s decision to keep risking Omega on further liberation raids.
characters.name: British prime minister

characters.description: A four-armed Konami accomplice who helped the former Signifier escape and accompanies him in disguise to Philo's execution. He shares an immediate interest in overthrowing the Ornu emperor.
characters.name: Konami accomplice

characters.description: A Marine sergeant in Alden Stone's boarding party. Funnybone joins the assault on an enemy artillery freighter and advances with the team toward its bridge.
characters.name: Funnybone

characters.description: A Marine in Alden Stone's boarding party. Termite joins the assault on an enemy artillery freighter and advances with the team toward its bridge.
characters.name: Termite

characters.description: A Roughback military leader whose ships arrive during Omega's battle at the desert mining world. His intervention confirms that Omega still has a powerful ally.
characters.name: Tull

characters.description: The new ruler of the Ornu after his father's assassination. Val considers him more dangerous and vengeful than his predecessor, making Omega and the human rebellion an immediate target.
characters.name: Young Ornu emperor

characters.description: A civilian representative of the Roughback survivors on Kotbulo. The elder recognizes Omega as a living entity in need of support and considers Bill's offer of a neighboring world.
characters.name: Roughback elder

characters.description: A Marine assigned to physical security while Bill and Bina enter the Occidental simulation. Guns remains outside with Funnybone beside their immobilized bodies.
characters.name: Guns

characters.description: The British prime minister whose movement demands that Omega stop taking further risks and carry its residents to a planet.
characters.name: Rose

characters.description: The leader of a delegation whose people are breaking with the Perseids and Ornu. The spokesperson offers Omega transport, repair platforms, intelligence, and logistical disruption rather than combat forces.
characters.name: Breakaway species spokesperson

characters.description: The Konami figure who helped the former Signifier escape. He commands a restored ancient facility and uses Voidlings while questioning his captive ally about Omega.
characters.name: Konami leader

characters.description: A senior bridge officer aboard Omega. Facing the occupied destination, Hans admits that he needs evidence the promised free life is real, yet chooses to continue with Bill.
characters.name: Hans Norder

characters.description: Commander of scouts from hidden human settlements founded by people who escaped the Langer 3 mining colony. Tim makes cautious first contact with Omega on behalf of the independent fleet.
characters.name: Tim Bowman

characters.description: Bill's grandfather and leader of the Langer 3 breakout. The hidden colonists identify him as the rebel whose actions allowed their ancestors to escape and build a free community.
characters.name: Corey Henderson

characters.description: Leader of the independent human colonies and their fleet. The commander explains how the settlements survived inside asteroids with limited ships, patched equipment, farming, and strict concealment from the Imperium.
characters.name: Colony commander

characters.description: A freeborn young woman from the hidden human colonies. She assists Miriam and Gordon during their visit and helps introduce them to the community created by Corey's rebellion.
characters.name: Young colony volunteer

characters.description: A Marine in Funnybone's lunar assault group. Tubes survives the destruction of the team's transport and the deliberate crash into the Voidling tunnel network.
characters.name: Tubes

characters.description: The identity of the Marine sergeant known as Funnybone. Sean Piker is killed by a Voidling tank's shockwave while leading the depleted lunar tunnel force.
characters.name: Sean Piker

characters.description: One of the entities associated with Omega. Val names Tobias as part of the group asking Bill for complete trust while an enemy boarding force moves through the ship.
characters.name: Tobias

characters.description: One of the entities associated with Omega. Val includes Judith among those asking Bill to trust them to defend him and the ship during the internal assault.
characters.name: Judith

recaps.ending: The allied fleet defeats the Voidlings at Azure and breaks the Ornu-Perseid invasion. Omega traps the Konami leader during his boarding attempt, disables the augmentations sustaining him, and survives his death. Funnybone and Splat die in the final campaign, while Bina survives an arm wound. Pertinax kills the young Ornu emperor during the retreat, then dies when the emperor activates his implanted kill switch. Eight months later, Azure is a functioning but hazardous settlement. Gordon Henderson has died, Miriam remains with the settlers, Hans Norder has become a fisherman, and Bina and Alden Stone carry much of the community's leadership. Bill can no longer enter Omega's sim space, but Val and Omega ask him to return as captain. After remaining through the settlement's anniversary and public farewell, he plans to leave with Omega, Val, Tobias, and Judith to protect humanity and investigate the continuing threats posed by the Imperium, the Warfang amalgam, and the Perseids.
recaps.in_short: Bill Henderson leads Omega through prison rescues and a search for a permanent human refuge while the Ornu succession, the Perseids, and a surviving Konami leader gather against him. Millions of abandoned people, Roughback allies, a breakaway species, and descendants of Corey Henderson's hidden colony rebellion join the migration. Their promised world, Azure, is occupied by parasitic Voidlings, forcing a combined battle on the moon, inside enemy ships, and aboard Omega. Funnybone and Splat die, but Omega kills the Konami leader and the allied fleet wins after Pertinax and the young emperor kill each other. Eight months later, Azure is a difficult but viable settlement and Gordon Henderson has died. Bina and Alden Stone lead much of the settlement work, while Bill agrees to depart after the anniversary with Omega, Val, Tobias, and Judith to guard humanity against unresolved external threats.

recaps.text: Previously: Bill Henderson commands the sentient warship Omega as humanity resists Ornu rule. The ship has become both a powerful weapon and a refuge for people escaping captivity. Bina Chakravarti serves among Bill's senior officers, while Alden Stone leads the Marines and Val advises Bill through Omega's simulated environment. Bill's family and companions have paid heavily for rebellion, and the struggle has left survivors divided over whether to keep fighting or seek safety. Omega now carries civilians as well as combatants, making every military decision a question of survival for the displaced human population.

Omega raids Ornu prison mines to free enslaved humans, but the first operation ends with overseers venting most prisoners before Stone's Marines can reach them. Bill refuses demands from civilian politicians to abandon the rescue campaign, although repeated short-range jumps threaten Omega's structure. At the Ornu capital, Pertinax avoids punishment for his earlier failure by proposing Consul Philo as a scapegoat. An escaped former Signifier and his disguised Konami ally watch as Philo is publicly executed. The former Signifier, who is Philo's nephew, turns toward revenge. Meanwhile, Bina rebuilds some trust by proposing an attack on a desert mining world used to exile inconvenient Ornu officials, and Bill approves the plan.

The desert-world attack becomes a trap. Omega faces an artillery freighter and waves of warships while Stone's Marines board the freighter. With fires spreading and the short-range jump drive near its limit, Bill prepares to abandon the boarding party if necessary. Civilian volunteers organize firefighting and medical aid, while political opponents quietly discuss surrender or a bridge takeover. Stone's team overcomes injuries and sealed hatches, captures the freighter's bridge, and turns its guns on the attackers. Tull's Roughback fleet arrives to destroy the remaining enemy ships. Omega escapes to Kotbulo for repairs, and the Marines take the damaged freighter separately after using it to bombard the Ornu settlement and create an opening for its human prisoners.

The former Ornu emperor is assassinated in his palace while the escaped former Signifier watches. His son takes the throne, purges rivals, kills his brother, and makes Omega his principal external target. Bill delays immediate settlement long enough to recruit allies, gaining a commitment from many Roughbacks but failing with two other potential partners. The Konami accomplice and the former Signifier recover a hidden craft and travel ahead to Omega's intended destination, where the Konami figure summons obedient sentient void servants. Bill and Bina also seek help from a species living almost entirely in simulation, but its moderators refuse to act. When Omega returns to the ruined Solar System, it discovers up to three million scattered human survivors. The ship faces an urgent mass evacuation while unidentified ships converge and some human stations threaten it.

Surrounded near Mars, Omega receives an offer from a delegation breaking with the Perseid-Ornu alignment. The new partners provide transports, repair capacity, intelligence, and logistical support, allowing part of Omega's population to disperse among their ships. When a mixed enemy fleet approaches, Omega cripples it, but Bill declines pursuit. Responsibility for roughly two million additional refugees has changed his priority from attacking the Imperial capital to securing a home. The senior crew accepts a plan to return to the allies, gather the Roughbacks, and then continue toward the promised system. Elsewhere, the Konami leader restores an ancient facility with Voidling labor, questions the former Signifier about Omega, and deploys extensive defenses around the destination.

During the journey, Rose seizes an allied transport with human collaborators and takes its crew hostage. Bill refuses to destroy the vessel or expend Omega's last safe jump to chase it. At the destination, scans reveal a defended world. Val explains that parasitic Voidlings destroyed the Konami and now control the planet, feeding on the suffering of host species. The alliance attacks before the orbital defenses can be completed, but fragmenting Voidling craft and lunar guns break its formation. Rose accepts the Konami leader's offer of power and gives Voidlings access to the captured ship. They drain and incapacitate him, while other vessels begin admitting the parasites. Refusing a victory that sacrifices allied crews, Bill orders a retreat.

A scouting party led by Tim Bowman contacts Omega from hidden human colonies descended from prisoners who escaped Langer 3 more than thirty years earlier. The colonists reveal that Bill's grandfather, Corey Henderson, led the breakout that made their survival possible. Their floating settlements have remained concealed inside asteroids, sustaining themselves with patched machinery, small farms, and a fleet of hundreds of craft. Gordon and Miriam witness the free community created by Corey's rebellion. Bill confronts Val for concealing this history. Val confirms that he aided Corey and shows Bill a record establishing that Corey's crew knowingly sacrificed itself so others could escape. Meanwhile, the young Ornu emperor accepts the Konami leader's military assistance but demands custody of the former Signifier, deepening the enemy alliance while preserving its internal distrust.

The young emperor reveals that the former Signifier carries a remote kill switch, coerces him for intelligence, and later kills him remotely to demonstrate his control over the invasion fleet. Bill's allies prepare a second Azure campaign with Marines, Roughbacks, colony pilots, and volunteers. Bina learns that the Konami leader may have survived through extensive biological augmentation. Omega returns to Azure and deploys the colony fleet against Voidling ships and hidden lunar guns. The Ornu-Perseid armada arrives before the surface threat is fully neutralized. A transport carrying Funnybone's lunar assault force appears destroyed, but a young colony pilot keeps her damaged shuttle flying long enough to crash deliberately into the tunnel network. Funnybone, Termite, Tubes, allied soldiers, and volunteers survive the impact and establish a foothold beneath the moon.

The ancient Konami leader takes command of a Perseid battleship and personally pursues Omega, revealing that augmentation sustained him after an earlier escape. The mixed allied formation suffers from enemy pressure and friendly-fire risk, but the colony pilots continue shielding the Roughbacks. Stone launches a separate infiltration using allied access codes. Splat salvages the damaged shuttle's approach by crashing through a Perseid hangar, leaving the force without an easy return. Tull's ship loses most of its asteroid armor, so he drives its exposed core into an Ornu battleship and begins a second boarding action. Stone's team advances through concealed Jackal ambushes, losing several volunteers and an allied fighter while Guns organizes the rear guard. Both internal assaults remain active as Omega draws enemy ships away from the allies.

In the lunar tunnels, the young colony volunteer helps Termite and the surviving assault force capture a Voidling tank, but its shockwave kills Funnybone, whose name is revealed as Sean Piker. The ground team continues and the moon's coil guns fall silent. Stone captures a Perseid ship, while Tull's boarding action and the colony fleet further weaken the enemy formation. The Konami leader openly breaks with the young emperor and prepares to board Omega under cover of a Voidling screen. Pertinax also defies the emperor and joins the attack, hoping to regain power. Bina recognizes the greater danger and secretly summons Stone back to Omega. Bill rejects Pertinax's demand for surrender, and Omega divides its dwindling firepower between the imperial flagship and the concealed boarding threat.

The Konami leader and a mixed force breach Omega, kill crew members, and advance through its shifting interior. Stone returns with Splat and Guns but finds his team trapped by the same reconfiguring corridors. In sim space, Val asks Bill to trust Omega, Judith, Tobias, and him completely. Omega then guides the invaders to the bridge and seals them inside. When the Konami leader attempts to take control, Omega disables the implants and enhancements sustaining his body. Stone's Marines attack the trapped force. Splat kills the invading Ornu officer before a Voidling explosive kills him, and Bina receives a nonfatal arm wound. The Konami leader dies as his augmentations fail. Outside, Pertinax kills the young emperor during the retreat, but the emperor activates Pertinax's kill switch before dying. Their deaths collapse Imperial command. The enemy fleet breaks, the Azure war ends, and Bill discovers that he can no longer enter sim space.

The survivors begin settling Azure. The young colony volunteer reaches the surface with Tim and their family, still grieving Sean Piker and the others killed in battle, while Termite has remained in contact during her recovery. Eight months later, the settlement operates through communal work and continues learning the hazards of an unfamiliar ecosystem. Hans Norder has chosen a life of fishing. Gordon Henderson dies after a decline, with Miriam and Bill having stepped back from public duties to care for him. Bina and Alden Stone assume much of the settlement's organizational burden. Although Bill cannot return to sim space, Val and Omega ask him to captain the ship again with Tobias and Judith. Bill agrees to leave Azure to protect humanity and investigate the Imperium, the Warfang amalgam, and the Perseids. At Bina's insistence, he will remain four more months for the settlement's anniversary and a public farewell.

characters.description: An exiled human entering a new zone where the ambient energy is initially lethal to him. Joe relies on ritual magic and his Reductionist path, but must first break the mortal limit before he can move or breathe safely.
characters.name: Joe

characters.description: The dwarven recruiter who forces Joe to choose a side in the local war. Captain presents himself as Joe's sponsor in the Dwarven Legion.
characters.name: Captain

characters.description: The elven representative at the recruitment area and the alternative to joining the dwarves. Enlightened One cannot act until Joe chooses voluntarily, but becomes the rejected faction recruiter once Joe commits to the dwarves.
characters.name: Enlightened One

characters.description: A dwarven Legion trainee in Joe's first local hunting party. Broski claims the leadership position, although Dudette makes the same claim and the party's hierarchy remains unsettled.
characters.name: Broski

characters.description: A dwarven Legion trainee assigned to Joe's first hunting party. Dudette also claims authority within the group, leaving its leadership unsettled when the new party first introduces itself.
characters.name: Dudette

characters.description: A dwarven Legion trainee introduced as a member of Joe's first local hunting party.
characters.name: Diane

characters.description: Joe's returning party member, recognized among a newly respawned cohort in Dwarven Legion training. His presence confirms that another of Joe's established companions has reached the dwarven zone.
characters.name: Jaxon

characters.description: A dwarven general who oversees the lethal officer-selection course. Mayhem admits the surviving candidates to a six-month test in which their rank depends on the measurable benefit they create for Dwarvenkind.
characters.name: Mayhem

characters.description: A magical researcher and Major General assigned as Joe's mentor and national liaison for the Ranker quest. Havoc has access to considerable military and magical resources.
characters.name: Havoc

characters.description: A grandmaster smith whose discarded failed shield attracts Joe's attention in the dwarven landfill. McPoundy prizes his professional reputation, and the unusual quest tied to the shield gives Joe a reason to seek him out.
characters.name: McPoundy

characters.description: A high-status elven opponent who attacks the Legion during its assault on a border fort. Havoc identifies this figure as Francine and treats her as an important rival.
characters.name: Elven rival

characters.description: The divine power whose hidden shrine Joe captures for his own faction. Establishing Occultatum in the zone changes the local religious balance, marks Joe as its champion, and turns his conflict with the elves into a blood feud.
characters.name: Occultatum

characters.description: A cat who enters Joe's room unhindered and then identifies herself as ruler of the hidden, neutral Nyanderthals. Cleocatra offers royal recognition for Joe's aid to one of her subjects and leaves him an unexplained reward.
characters.name: Cleocatra

characters.description: A Nyanderthal subject whom Joe previously saved. A letter concerning Cindy Clawford brings Queen Cleocatra to Joe and establishes that his assistance has earned formal recognition from the hidden neutral people.
characters.name: Cindy Clawford

characters.description: A dwarven princess seeking the high-priestess position in Occultatum's new faith. She offers a Grand Temple and additional fort temples, viewing the religious office as both a holy calling and relief from dynastic pressure.
characters.name: Third dwarven princess

characters.description: A human arcane loot lord and Odds and Ends shopkeeper who delivers equipment that Havoc arranged for Joe. Minya also reports a connection to the shop's counterpart on Midgard.
characters.name: Minya

characters.description: A forge-capable elemental summoned and bound by Joe in the Caves of Solitude. The slag elemental obeys while Joe sustains their mana link and supplies intense heat for field crafting.
characters.name: Slag elemental

characters.description: The name Joe gives his bound slag elemental before dismissing the summon to conserve mana.
characters.name: Slagathor

characters.description: The commander of the hidden elven fort who maintains its grand illusion defenses. The Lady of Light captures Joe after his sabotage and arranges to confine and interrogate him inside the fort.
characters.name: Lady of Light

characters.description: An elven interrogator who restrains Joe with mana-suppressing cuffs. Eli repeatedly kills and respawns his prisoner while using speech-based compulsion to demand equipment and information.
characters.name: Eli

characters.description: A sanctioned necromancer and Legion officer who supplies volunteers for Joe's anti-illusion ritual. Major Infraction cooperates despite open hostility because the coming fort assault requires a defense against elven deception.
characters.name: Major Infraction

characters.description: Major Infraction's axe-specialist officer, assigned to escort Joe into the assault on Grandma's Shoe. Captain Cleavage accepts Joe's painful anti-illusion protection before they enter the contested fort.
characters.name: Captain Cleavage

characters.description: A dwarven officer who challenges Joe's authority to consume oligarchy resources during the volcanic emergency. General Information changes course when Joe explains the rescue plan and commits mana-rich officers to the effort.
characters.name: General Information

recaps.ending: The dwarves capture Grandma's Shoe after Joe's Ritual of Argus helps key fighters resist the fort's illusions. Havoc kills the Lady of Light, but the collapsing Prismatic Evergreen threatens to trigger the volcano and convert the fallen through an elven respawn point. Joe frees Havoc from a sensory prison, escapes with Jaxon and Captain Cleavage, and then organizes the Legion to construct Pharaoh's Pyramid of Panaceas, stopping the eruption. After the numbered chapters, Joe gains the fort, its Ledger of Souls, a command, land, cleared crimes, and promotion to level-21 Major General. He restores Havoc's daughter Francine through the ledger, proving that she was not the slain elven commander. Havoc can also be restored and accepts Joe as his apprentice. Joe plans to develop his new base while the war continues, but he cannot claim the artifact alchemy structure until he reaches master alchemist rank.
recaps.in_short: Exiled into a zone divided by war, Joe survives its lethal ambient power, joins the dwarves, and pursues an officer candidacy through ritual engineering. He develops aspect crafting, survives the capital's landfill, helps capture a minor fort, establishes Occultatum in dwarven territory, and gains advanced ritual-orb training. His investigation of supposed spirits uncovers a hidden elven fortress beneath Grandma's Shoe. After escaping its prison, he warns the dwarves and creates the costly Ritual of Argus to counter its illusions. Havoc kills the Lady of Light during the assault, while Joe prevents the fort's volcano from erupting by building Pharaoh's Pyramid of Panaceas. In the epilogue, Joe receives Grandma's Shoe and promotion to Major General, restores Havoc's true daughter Francine, and becomes Havoc's apprentice. The elven war remains active, and the new artifact workshop cannot be claimed until Joe becomes a master alchemist.

recaps.text: Previously: Joe enters this volume as an exile from the prior zone, carrying the abilities of a Ritualist, Ritual Architect, and Reductionist into unfamiliar territory. His established connections remain on Midgard, including the Wanderers and his returning party member Jaxon. The exile prevents an immediate return and forces Joe to confront the next zone on its own terms.

So far this book: The new zone's ambient energy repeatedly kills Joe until he completes an internal mana pattern, breaks the mortal limit, and gains enough physical capacity to function. Hostile recruiters force him to choose between the dwarves and elves, and he joins the dwarves. Captain enrolls him in the Legion and explains that forts control local respawns in a war where native deaths in enemy territory can convert a person into the opposing race. During compulsory training, Joe serves as healer and support for Broski, Dudette, and Diane on a stone lizard hunt. He eventually breaks the training compulsion after nearly a month and discovers Jaxon among another dwarven cohort. What appears to be a fort raid then becomes a lethal officer-selection course.

Joe survives officer selection by demonstrating his unusual ritual and crafting background. General Mayhem grants him a six-month Ranker quest in which his future rank depends on the benefit he creates for Dwarvenkind. The Candidate title freezes his reputation until final judgment, and Major General Havoc becomes his mentor and liaison. Havoc recognizes the importance of Joe's Ritual Architect and Reductionist paths and begins considering how they might contribute to the war. Early experiments show that Reductionist crafting breaks materials into dangerous aspects that require specialized storage. Joe also discovers that his old supplies have been compressed into a damaged cube. A system tutorial teaches him how to use aspects for alchemy, smithing, enchanting, and rituals, while warning that advanced creations need suitable knowledge and energy from bound cores.

Havoc sends Joe into the toxic landfill beneath the dwarven capital as a survival test and a source of crafting material. Joe develops rituals that clear low-rank refuse, gathers aspects and cores, and discovers both illegally dumped corpses producing undead and a malfunctioning Hidden Guardian deep below the city. His overreach causes a collapse and a fatal encounter, but he completes the test. Havoc then admits that ordinary achievements will not overcome political resistance to Joe's noble ambitions. Joe must create something capable of taking an elven fort. He designs a mana-withering ritual intended to disable both a fort's plant guardian and its spellcasters. When the elves seize a border fort, Havoc mobilizes an immediate counterattack under Joe's candidacy, leaving the untested ritual as the central plan.

Joe's wall-breaking ritual opens the captured fort, and his mana-withering design weakens its defenders and plant guardian. Havoc completes the conquest, though an important elven rival escapes. Joe then saves an injured cat, is captured by elves, and follows them to a hidden travel shrine. By claiming it for Occultatum, he introduces another divine power into the zone and earns a blood feud with the elves. The fort victory clears his debts and brings him to McPoundy, Havoc's grandmaster-smith brother. Joe proves his Reductionist ability by destroying one of McPoundy's notorious failures, winning the smith's attention and the prospect of a custom weapon. His military success has advanced his candidacy, but Havoc also imposes an obligation concerning the elven mage he believes may be the lost Francine.

Queen Cleocatra reveals that the cat in Joe's room is ruler of the hidden, neutral Nyanderthals. Her reward includes a sage-ranked weapon template. Meanwhile, a dwarven princess becomes Occultatum's high priestess and helps convert the capital's Grand Temple, making Joe champion of the dominant dwarven religious faction. McPoundy trades advanced instruction for access to Cleocatra's design and produces an expert version: six ritual orbs with control cuffs. Joe can bind abilities or ritual patterns into the orbs, but controlling several at once is difficult and their destruction carries serious penalties. Havoc continues harsh physical training, then orders Joe out to gain a level, kill elves, or return with important intelligence. Minya supplies delayed equipment for that assignment, including protection and support for his exotic new weapon.

Investigating reports of dangerous air spirits near Grandma's Shoe, Joe enters the Caves of Solitude and improves his methods for storing and transferring aspects. He summons a slag elemental for mobile forge work, then discovers that the supposed spirits are earth elementals being moved by elven summoners. Following their route reveals a major elven fort hidden inside an active volcano near the dwarven capital. Joe infiltrates it and attacks the crystal structures sustaining its camouflage. The Lady of Light captures him and confines him on an island surrounded by magma, where Eli uses suppressing cuffs, repeated deaths, and compulsive speech magic to interrogate him. Uncontained unique aspects kill Eli and restore Joe's magic. Joe escapes through the magma, improvises a heat-draining ritual to tunnel out, and finally reaches a normal respawn point with proof of the concealed invasion force.

Joe reports the hidden fort and its invasion plan to Occultatum's high priestess, who mobilizes the dwarven oligarchy under his candidate authority. Havoc identifies the fort's illusion structure as the Prismatic Evergreen and commits to an assault. Joe develops reproducible mana batteries, but they cannot be deployed quickly enough for the immediate battle. Instead, he gathers aspects and constructs the Ritual of Argus to counter the elven illusions. The first activation incapacitates its donors. A second attempt uses thousands of Legion volunteers, kills many when unstable circles fail, and grants a limited number of people the Eye of Argus for seven days. Major Infraction holds Joe responsible for the losses but accepts the protection's military value.

Havoc's micro-golems breach Grandma's Shoe while Joe and Captain Cleavage use Eye of Argus to resist the fort's illusions. Joe finds Jaxon beneath magical rubble, frees and heals him, and gives him the same protection. The three recognize that the apparent dwarven victory remains an illusion and reach the Prismatic Evergreen's control room. Havoc confronts the Lady of Light, whom he calls Francine despite her rejection of that identity. She reveals that destroying the tree will trigger the volcano and redirect the dead into elven respawns. Havoc kills her but is caught in a sensory-deprivation spell. Joe releases him, escapes with Jaxon and Captain Cleavage before Havoc overloads, and organizes the Legion to reduce the fort's materials into construction aspects. Using the enemy commander's master core and an artifact blueprint, Joe builds Pharaoh's Pyramid of Panaceas and stabilizes the volcano. The fort is taken, although Joe cannot claim the new alchemy structure without master rank.

characters.description: A private investigator and committed marijuana smoker living in the beach community of Gordita Beach in 1970. His loose manner and fading counterculture surroundings conceal persistence, professional instincts, and a network reaching from surfers and musicians to police and prosecutors.
characters.name: Larry Sportello

characters.description: Doc's former girlfriend, who unexpectedly returns to ask for his help. She is now involved with wealthy developer Mickey Wolfmann and fears that a plan by Mickey's wife and her lover will remove him from the way.
characters.name: Shasta Fay Hepworth

characters.description: A powerful Los Angeles real-estate developer whose projects have transformed large stretches of the coast. Shasta says he has recently begun questioning his wealth and that people close to him intend to have him confined.
characters.name: Mickey Wolfmann

characters.description: Mickey Wolfmann's wife. According to Shasta, Sloane and her lover are discussing a scheme to have Mickey declared mentally unfit and placed in an institution.
characters.name: Sloane Wolfmann

characters.description: Doc's friend and neighbor, whose mystical outlook makes her attentive to hidden connections and shifts in the atmosphere of Gordita Beach. She works as an informal receptionist and sounding board around his investigations.
characters.name: Sortilège

characters.description: A perpetually relaxed friend in Doc's beach circle. Denis often appears when Doc needs company, transportation, food, or information carried through Gordita Beach's informal network.
characters.name: Denis

characters.description: An LAPD detective who alternates police work with appearances in commercials and television. He treats Doc as both suspect and useful outsider, sustaining a hostile, competitive familiarity with him across the boundary between official and private investigation.
characters.name: Christian Bjornsen

characters.description: An employee at Chick Planet Massage, a business operating on one of Mickey Wolfmann's developments. Her warnings and fragmentary information make her an uneasy contact in Doc's search for the missing developer.
characters.name: Jade

characters.description: A Black ex-convict who hires Doc to find Glen Charlock, a white supremacist connected to Mickey Wolfmann. Tariq says an unresolved obligation from their time in prison gives him reason to locate Charlock.
characters.name: Tariq Khalil

characters.description: A former heroin user raising her daughter after the reported death of her musician husband, Coy. Troubled by signs that he may still be alive, she asks Doc to discover what has happened to him.
characters.name: Hope Harlingen

characters.description: A saxophonist whose supposed overdose left Hope Harlingen a widow and their daughter without a father. Evidence that he survived makes him the center of one of Doc's overlapping missing-person cases.
characters.name: Coy Harlingen

characters.description: A deputy district attorney and Doc's intermittent lover. She can move through records and institutions closed to him, though their personal connection is complicated by her place inside the legal system he distrusts.
characters.name: Penny Kimball

characters.description: A maritime lawyer, occasional musician, and old friend of Doc. His knowledge of ships and waterfront law helps Doc investigate the Golden Fang, a mysterious schooner associated with the cases.
characters.name: Sauncho Smilax

characters.description: A dentist with a taste for cocaine who works within the Golden Fang network of dental offices. His mixture of professional respectability and criminal connections reflects the organization Doc is trying to understand.
characters.name: Rudy Blatnoyd

characters.description: A violent associate from Shasta's time around Mickey Wolfmann. His name recurs in accounts linking the Wolfmann disappearance, Glen Charlock's death, and the criminal interests surrounding the Golden Fang.
characters.name: Puck Beaverton

characters.description: A feared loan collector and police informant with a long record of violence. Evidence connecting him to several deaths makes him a dangerous focus of Doc's late investigation.
characters.name: Adrian Prussia

recaps.ending: Bigfoot's indirect guidance leads Doc to Adrian Prussia, a protected police informant connected to the death of Bigfoot's former partner and to Puck Beaverton. Doc survives the confrontation in Adrian's fortified hideout; Adrian and Puck die. The aftermath leaves Doc with a large quantity of heroin belonging to the Golden Fang. Rather than sell it or accept a wealthy client's payment, he uses it as leverage: through Crocker Fenway, he returns the drugs in exchange for Coy Harlingen's release from the covert obligations that have kept him away from Hope and their daughter. Coy is able to go home. Mickey Wolfmann has already returned to public life and his former business identity, while the full machinery behind his disappearance remains beyond any clean legal resolution. Shasta also returns, but she and Doc do not restore their old relationship to certainty. Doc finally drives into a dense fog, moving with other cars until visibility improves. The open road preserves the novel's uncertainty, but his choice on Coy's behalf provides one concrete rescue from the system he has traced.
recaps.in_short: In 1970 Los Angeles, private investigator Doc Sportello is asked by his former girlfriend Shasta to protect developer Mickey Wolfmann from a plan to have him confined. Mickey and Shasta disappear, and Doc is found unconscious beside the murdered Glen Charlock. New cases converge: Tariq Khalil wants Charlock found, while Hope Harlingen believes her supposedly dead husband Coy is alive. Coy proves to be an informant trapped inside overlapping police and political operations. The Golden Fang appears in multiple forms—a schooner, a dental syndicate, and a channel for narcotics and influence—while Mickey is taken to a treatment center and returned to his old capitalist life. Shasta eventually reappears but offers no stable explanation or reunion. Evidence draws Doc to violent informant Adrian Prussia and Puck Beaverton; both die in the confrontation. Doc then trades recovered Golden Fang heroin for Coy's freedom rather than taking a payoff, allowing Coy to return to Hope and their daughter. With the larger network intact and Shasta still elusive, Doc drives into the California fog.

recaps.text: In Gordita Beach in 1970, private investigator Doc Sportello receives an unexpected visit from his former girlfriend Shasta Fay Hepworth. She is involved with real-estate developer Mickey Wolfmann and says Mickey's wife Sloane and her lover plan to have him declared incompetent and confined. Doc follows the lead to Chick Planet Massage, located in one of Wolfmann's developments. He is knocked unconscious and wakes outside beside the body of Glen Charlock, a white supremacist who worked as Mickey's guard. LAPD detective Bigfoot Bjornsen treats Doc as a suspect. Mickey and Shasta both vanish. Separate clients add to the same puzzle: Tariq Khalil wants Charlock located over an old prison obligation, and Hope Harlingen asks about signs that her saxophonist husband Coy, officially dead from an overdose, may still be alive. What begins as a favor for Shasta has become linked cases involving murder and two missing men.

Doc's contacts widen the investigation beyond Mickey's development. Maritime lawyer Sauncho Smilax helps identify the Golden Fang, a schooner with a suspicious history. The same name belongs to a network of dental offices, including the practice of cocaine-using dentist Rudy Blatnoyd, suggesting a business structure that crosses legitimate and criminal worlds. Coy Harlingen makes contact and confirms that he is alive. He has been separated from Hope and their daughter while working as an informant, moving through groups monitored or manipulated by law enforcement. His assignments overlap with the forces around Mickey Wolfmann. Doc cannot yet tell whether the Golden Fang is one organization, several connected operations, or a name adopted for different parts of the same system, but Shasta's disappearance, Mickey's abduction, Charlock's death, and Coy's captivity no longer look independent.

Following Coy's clues, Doc traces Mickey to Chryskylodon, a private treatment center where confinement, therapy, surveillance, and political pressure blend together. Mickey's recent desire to give away part of his fortune had threatened the interests built around him. By the time he emerges, that impulse has been erased or suppressed, and he returns to his familiar role as a developer. Coy remains trapped in informant work and unable to go openly home. Other inquiries show the Golden Fang operating through respectable fronts while narcotics, property, policing, and private coercion support one another. Deaths among people tied to the network remove possible witnesses rather than producing clarity. Doc has located Mickey, but the original client, Shasta, is still absent, and solving one disappearance has exposed a structure too distributed to confront as a single culprit.

Shasta returns to Gordita Beach after her unexplained absence. She describes time spent in Mickey's orbit and aboard the Golden Fang, but her performance of indifference leaves Doc unable to separate confession, provocation, and concealment. Their intimacy resumes briefly without restoring the relationship they once had. Doc continues connecting Glen Charlock's murder to Puck Beaverton, a violent figure associated with Shasta and Mickey. Meanwhile, Bigfoot's erratic hostility increasingly appears bound to his own unresolved grief over the death of his former police partner. Official files and unofficial hints point beyond Puck toward Adrian Prussia, a brutal loan collector and protected informant. The case has narrowed from the diffuse Golden Fang network to men who commit violence within it and receive protection from authorities.

Doc follows the lead to Adrian Prussia's fortified base, where Puck Beaverton is also present. Adrian's value as a police informant has allowed his violence to continue, and the trail connects him not only to Doc's investigation but to the killing of Bigfoot's former partner. The visit turns into a lethal confrontation. Doc escapes, while Adrian and Puck die. The result closes off the most immediate threat but offers no lawful exposure of the system that protected them. In the aftermath, Doc comes into possession of a large cache of heroin belonging to the Golden Fang. The drugs give him leverage over an organization that has otherwise remained too fluid and well connected for his investigation to reach.

Doc uses the recovered heroin to secure the only release still within reach. He arranges through the wealthy and well-connected Crocker Fenway to return the Golden Fang's property on the condition that Coy Harlingen be freed from his informant obligations. Doc declines a financial reward, and Coy is able to return to Hope and their daughter. Mickey Wolfmann has resumed his old public and business identity; whatever idealistic change prompted his removal has not survived. Shasta is back but remains emotionally elusive, and her connection with Doc is unresolved rather than renewed. Bigfoot's role in guiding Doc toward Adrian has also served the detective's private need for vengeance without bringing institutional accountability. With individual mysteries partly answered but the larger network intact, Doc drives into thick coastal fog, joining a slow line of cars until the road becomes visible again.

characters.description: The Dragon Rider bonded to Saphira, now a seasoned warrior and the Varden's greatest hope. Bearing the sword Brisingr and the accumulated training of the elves, he leads and fights at the front of the rebellion as it drives toward the Empire's heart, knowing that only he and Saphira might stand against the tyrant king in the end.
characters.name: Eragon

characters.description: Eragon's blue dragon and partner, mighty in battle and fiercely proud, one of the last free dragons in the world. She carries Eragon into war, shares his every thought, and understands that the survival of dragonkind itself may rest on how the coming struggle ends.
characters.name: Saphira

characters.description: Eragon's cousin, now a bold and resourceful captain in the Varden, married to Katrina. Fighting with a hammer and a sharp tactical mind, he wins hard victories for the rebellion and is prepared to risk everything for his family and the cause.
characters.name: Roran

characters.description: Roran's wife, rescued from the Empire's servants, steadfast and courageous as she follows the Varden's war and awaits the child she and Roran are expecting.
characters.name: Katrina

characters.description: The commanding leader of the Varden, guiding the alliance of humans, dwarves, elves, and others in a bid to topple the Empire. Brave and politically astute, she bears enormous personal risk to keep the rebellion moving toward the capital and the king who rules it.
characters.name: Nasuada

characters.description: The elf envoy and warrior, close ally and companion to Eragon. Reserved, principled, and deadly in a fight, she carries heavy responsibilities for her people as the war reaches its climax and the fate of the elves is drawn into the balance.
characters.name: Arya

characters.description: Eragon's estranged kin, a Rider of the red dragon Thorn, enslaved to the king by binding oaths. Powerful, resentful, and trapped, he serves the Empire against his will and stands as one of the last great obstacles between the Varden and victory.
characters.name: Murtagh

characters.description: Eragon's dwarf friend, now king of his people, bringing the dwarves' strength to the alliance. Loyal and steadfast, he leads his nation into the decisive stage of the war against the Empire.
characters.name: Orik

characters.description: The tyrant king of the Empire, an ancient renegade Dragon Rider of overwhelming sorcerous power hoarded over generations. The final enemy of the cycle, he rules from his fortress capital through fear, enslaved servants, and unbreakable oaths, and confronting him is the last and gravest task the Varden face.
characters.name: Galbatorix

recaps.ending: The cycle ends in victory bought at great cost and lasting change. The Varden and their allies breach the Empire's capital, and Murtagh and Thorn, finding the strength to free themselves from the king's oaths at the crucial moment, break with Galbatorix. In the final confrontation Eragon defeats the king not with a stronger blade but with a spell that makes Galbatorix experience all the pain and grief he has inflicted across his long reign; overwhelmed, the king unmakes himself with a word. With the tyrant gone, Nasuada takes the throne to rebuild the shattered realm, and Arya, after the death of her mother, becomes queen of the elves and bonds with a newly hatched green dragon, becoming a Rider herself. Roran and Katrina welcome their daughter. But the surviving dragon eggs and the many Eldunari cannot be kept safe within Alagaesia, so Eragon accepts that he must leave his homeland forever to raise a new generation of dragons and Riders in a distant place. He parts from Arya, from Roran, and from all he has known, and sails away into exile as the guardian of dragonkind's future, while Murtagh and Thorn depart north to find their own peace.
recaps.in_short: The Varden fight their way across the Empire, taking city after city as Eragon and Saphira lead and Roran wins hard battles. Seeking the power to match the king, Eragon and Saphira journey in secret to the ruined Rider island of Vroengard, where they gain a great hoard of Eldunari, the preserved hearts that hold dragons' minds, along with a hidden cache of dragon eggs, and Eragon discovers his own true name. At the capital, the alliance breaks the city's defenses, and Eragon, Saphira, and Arya confront Galbatorix and his enslaved Rider Murtagh. Rather than defeat the king by strength alone, Eragon casts a spell that forces Galbatorix to feel the full weight of all the suffering he has caused, and the king, unable to bear it, destroys himself. In the aftermath Nasuada becomes ruler, Arya is made queen of the elves and Rider to a new dragon, and Eragon, with no safe place in the land to raise the surviving eggs and Eldunari, leaves Alagaesia forever to found a new order of Riders elsewhere.

recaps.text: Across the earlier books, Eragon became a Dragon Rider bonded to Saphira, lost his uncle and mentor Brom to the Empire, and joined the Varden, the rebels fighting King Galbatorix. He trained with the hidden elf Rider Oromis and his dragon Glaedr, was transformed by elven magic, and destroyed the Shade Durza. His cousin Roran rose among the rebels and married Katrina after Eragon freed her and killed the king's servants, the Ra'zac. Nasuada came to lead the Varden. Eragon learned that his father was Brom rather than the traitor Morzan, forged his own sword Brisingr, and saw his friend Orik crowned dwarf king. The enslaved Rider Murtagh, on the red dragon Thorn, remained a bitter enemy under the king's control, and in battle he and Galbatorix's borrowed power killed Oromis and Glaedr, though the old dragon's preserved heart-of-hearts passed to Eragon and Saphira as the war neared its climax.

This final book opens with the Varden pressing their campaign against the Empire, capturing fortified cities as they advance toward the capital and the king. Eragon and Saphira, hardened by years of war and grief, lead the rebellion's fight, while Roran wins battles as a trusted captain and Nasuada steers the alliance of humans, dwarves, and elves. Everyone understands that Galbatorix, hoarding immense power in his stronghold, is far stronger than any of them, and that some decisive advantage or stroke will be needed if the tyrant is to be overthrown. The stage is set for the last and hardest phase of the long war.

characters.description: A high school student in Connecticut who lives with her older half-sister and sleeps in her car on the nights their apartment is unbearable. Her mother died two years ago, her father surfaces only when he wants money, and she keeps herself afloat on diner shifts, a strict budget, and a plan built around scholarships and a gift for numbers. Guarded and self-reliant, she is used to counting on nobody and to noticing everything. Her mornings begin with a game of chess in the park against an old man she has never beaten. She has never heard of the Hawthorne family.
characters.name: Avery Kylie Grambs

characters.description: Avery's older half-sister and the only steady adult in her life: a diner worker who bakes elaborate cupcakes, dyes the ends of her hair in bright colors, and takes in strays of every kind. Warm and forgiving to a fault, she is dating a possessive boyfriend whose presence is the reason Avery often sleeps somewhere else.
characters.name: Libby Grambs

characters.description: An old man living on the street near Avery's usual route, who meets her each morning for a game of chess in the park. He will accept the breakfast she brings but never money, deflects every question about his past, and has never lost to her.
characters.name: Harry

characters.description: Avery's best friend, blunt, loyal, and endlessly entertained by other people's disasters. Her parents monitor her phone and email, so she swears in elaborate substitutions. She is the one person Avery tells everything.
characters.name: Maxine Liu

characters.description: The second of the four Hawthorne grandsons, raised from childhood as the one who would inherit the family empire and run it. Formal, controlled, and accustomed to being obeyed, he appears at Avery's school before she has any idea who he is, to take her measure and warn her away from his family.
characters.name: Grayson Hawthorne

characters.description: A self-made Texas billionaire, dead before the story begins, who built a fortune out of nothing and spent decades extending Hawthorne House into a maze of wings, passages, and hidden rooms. He raised his four grandsons on riddles and games set every Saturday morning, and he left a will that gives his own family almost nothing and his fortune to a stranger.
characters.name: Tobias Hawthorne

characters.description: The young lawyer assigned to Avery by the firm that has represented the Hawthorne family for decades. Precise, ambitious, and relentlessly practical, she treats the inheritance as an estate to be defended and Avery's public image as an asset to be managed.
characters.name: Alisa Ortega

characters.description: Tobias Hawthorne's former head of security, reassigned to Avery the moment the will is read. Blunt, watchful, and unsentimental, he treats every threat as real and expects to be obeyed on anything touching her safety.
characters.name: Oren

characters.description: The third Hawthorne grandson, restless and drawn to risk, brought up to treat the world as a series of puzzles with a way to win hidden inside. He is the first to decide that Avery is not an accident but his grandfather's last game, and he wants to play it with her.
characters.name: Jameson Winchester Hawthorne

characters.description: The youngest Hawthorne grandson, cheerful, talkative, and forever building elaborate contraptions out of whatever the house contains. He is the easiest of the brothers to like and the quickest to treat Avery as a person rather than a problem.
characters.name: Alexander Hawthorne

characters.description: The oldest Hawthorne grandson, who left the family's world years ago for odd jobs and long drives and speaks like a man who has spent time on a ranch. He appoints himself peacekeeper between his brothers and takes an immediate protective interest in the newcomers.
characters.name: Nash Hawthorne

characters.description: Tobias Hawthorne's younger daughter and the mother of the four brothers, theatrical, charming, and entirely unbothered by other people's boundaries. She named each of her sons after the man she said had fathered him, and she is openly certain the fortune should have been hers.
characters.name: Skye Hawthorne

characters.description: Tobias Hawthorne's elder daughter, composed and formidable, married into a wealthy family and long positioned as the one who kept the household in order. She begins looking for a legal route to overturn her father's will within minutes of hearing it read.
characters.name: Zara Hawthorne-Calligaris

characters.description: The granddaughter of the couple who run Hawthorne House, quiet and careful, still visibly grieving the older sister she lost the year before. She grew up around the Hawthorne brothers and knows more about their history than she volunteers.
characters.name: Rebecca Laughlin

characters.description: Tobias Hawthorne's only son, who died roughly twenty years ago in a fire on the family's private island that also killed several of his friends. The household does not speak of him, and the search for what happened to him is treated as closed.
characters.name: Toby Hawthorne

characters.description: Rebecca's older sister, who died about a year before Avery arrives. Vivid, admired, and drawn to danger, she was involved with both Grayson and Jameson at the same time, and her death left the two brothers estranged, each privately certain he was to blame.
characters.name: Emily Laughlin

recaps.ending: The attempts on Avery's life were arranged by Skye Hawthorne, who recruited Libby's former boyfriend Drake in the belief that Avery's death would return the fortune to her sons. Drake corners Avery inside the house and Oren kills him; Skye is taken into custody. With that settled, Avery finishes the trail her benefactor left and confirms that Toby Hawthorne survived the fire on the family's island and has lived unfound ever since. Looking at a picture of the missing man, she recognizes him: Harry, the homeless chess player she has faced across a board every morning for months, is Tobias Hawthorne's son. Why she was chosen is still unanswered, and the connection appears to run through her dead mother and the secret her mother said she was keeping about the day Avery was born. Avery decides to stay at Hawthorne House for the rest of the year and to play the game out. Jameson is her partner in it and something more; Grayson holds himself at a deliberate distance; Nash has attached himself to Libby's welfare; Xander is simply glad she is staying. Zara's challenge to the will has not dislodged her, but the family is nowhere near reconciled, and the questions of where Toby is and why Avery was chosen are both wide open.
recaps.in_short: Avery Kylie Grambs, a Connecticut teenager scraping by on diner shifts and scholarship plans, is summoned to Texas for the reading of a billionaire's will and learns that Tobias Hawthorne, a man she never met, has left her almost his entire fortune. His two daughters and his four grandsons get almost nothing, and Avery must live in the family's puzzle-box mansion for a year to keep it. Certain that his grandfather never acted without a reason, Jameson Hawthorne enlists her to work out why she was chosen, and the trail runs through the house's hidden passages and the family's buried history: the death of a girl both Jameson and Grayson loved, and the fire that supposedly killed the old man's only son. Someone wants Avery dead. She is shot at on the grounds and the wing where she sleeps is set alight, and the attacks turn out to have been arranged by the brothers' mother, Skye, through Libby's ex-boyfriend, who is killed in the attempt. Avery ends the book knowing that Toby Hawthorne is alive, and that he is the old man she has been playing chess with all along.

recaps.text: Avery Kylie Grambs is a high school student in Connecticut with a talent for mathematics and no safety net. Her mother died two years ago, her father surfaces only when he needs something, and she and her older half-sister Libby scrape by on diner wages. Avery sleeps in her car on the nights Libby's boyfriend Drake makes the apartment intolerable, keeps to a strict budget, and pins everything on graduating early and winning scholarships. Her closest friend is Maxine Liu, whose parents monitor her phone. Every morning before school Avery plays chess in the park with an old homeless man called Harry, bringing him the breakfast he will accept and offering money he will not, and losing to him every time. She knows nothing at all about a family named Hawthorne.

A polished stranger named Grayson Hawthorne turns up at Avery's school to warn her away from his family, which is the first she has heard of them. A law firm then flies her and Libby to Texas for the reading of the will of Tobias Hawthorne, a self-made billionaire she has never met. The reading takes place at Hawthorne House, an enormous mansion the old man spent decades extending into a warren of wings, passages, and hidden rooms. His daughters, the controlled Zara and the theatrical Skye, and his four grandsons expect to inherit; instead they receive token bequests, and nearly the entire fortune goes to Avery. The conditions are that she live in Hawthorne House for a year and that the family keep the right to live there with her. Libby comes along as her guardian. Avery acquires a lawyer, Alisa Ortega, a head of security, Oren, and four hostile Hawthorne brothers: Nash, Grayson, Jameson, and Xander, all of them raised on the puzzles their grandfather set them every Saturday of their childhood.

Avery moves into Hawthorne House under guard while the press camps at the gates and the country decides she is a fraud or a gold digger. The family treats her as a problem to be solved or removed: Zara looks for grounds to break the will, Skye works on her sons, and the staff keep their distance. Jameson is the exception. He is convinced that his grandfather never did anything without a reason, that Avery is the last game the old man ever built, and that the two of them should play it together, and he draws her into hunting for the answer through the house's hidden passages. Xander offers cheerful help, Nash watches out for Libby and Avery both, and Grayson keeps his distance while making plain that he blames her for what his family has lost. Avery begins to wonder whether the answer lies in her own past, and remembers her mother once telling her she had a secret about the day Avery was born. Anonymous threats start to arrive.

Following the clues left for them, Jameson and Avery uncover the family's fault lines. Both Jameson and Grayson had been involved with Emily Laughlin, the granddaughter of the couple who run the house, and her death about a year ago drove the brothers apart, each certain he had caused it. Emily's sister Rebecca is still living with the loss. Avery, meanwhile, finds evidence that Tobias Hawthorne knew a great deal about her long before he died, which convinces her the choice was deliberate rather than random. The danger stops being theoretical when a shot is fired at her on the grounds. Oren tightens security and treats everyone with access to the estate as a suspect. Avery and Jameson grow closer as they play, and Grayson pulls further away.

The clue trail leads into the part of the family's history nobody will discuss: Tobias Hawthorne's son Toby, who died roughly twenty years ago in a fire on the family's private island that also killed several of his friends. The more Avery learns about Toby, the more her benefactor's arrangements look like a message rather than a whim. Zara's legal challenge advances, Skye keeps circling her sons and Avery alike, and Libby's former boyfriend Drake turns up in Texas. In public Avery is coached and managed by Alisa; inside the house she and the brothers work the puzzle. She becomes convinced that the reason she was chosen is tied to her mother, and that her mother's secret and the Hawthorne family are the same story.

Someone sets fire to the wing where Avery sleeps and she barely gets out. Oren's investigation makes it plain that whoever wants her dead has access to the house, so the family's whereabouts matter more than their manners. Avery refuses to leave: walking away would forfeit the inheritance and end any chance of an answer. The brothers close ranks around her, Grayson included despite himself, and the clues Tobias Hawthorne planted begin to fit together into a single trail pointing at his supposedly dead son.

The trail leads out of the house and into the twenty-year-old story of the island fire, where the version the family has always told stops matching the records Tobias Hawthorne kept for himself. Avery also finds the link she has been chasing between the Hawthornes and her own mother, and understands that the old man's choice of her was a decision made years in advance rather than an act of charity. The attacks escalate at the same time, and Oren narrows the danger to someone with a direct interest in returning the fortune to the Hawthorne family.

The attempts on Avery's life prove to have been arranged by Skye Hawthorne, who recruited Libby's former boyfriend Drake for the work, believing that Avery's death would send the fortune back to her sons. Drake corners Avery inside the house and Oren kills him; Skye is arrested. Avery then finishes her benefactor's trail and confirms that Toby Hawthorne survived the island fire and has been living unfound for twenty years. Shown a picture of the missing man, she recognizes Harry, the homeless chess player from her own neighborhood, and understands that she has spent months sitting across a board from Tobias Hawthorne's son. Why she was chosen is still unanswered, and the connection runs through her dead mother. Avery commits to staying out the year at Hawthorne House and finishing the game, with Jameson beside her, Grayson deliberately apart, Nash looking after Libby, and the family still divided over her.
